segments.text: Come in. I am Dr. Villidsen. We have not met before, I think.
No, we have not. Louise Dahl. Lovely to meet you.
I was just saying to the lady outside that the waiting room went far quicker than I expected.
That is good to hear.
Take a seat. There is a lot on your list today, so I would like to go through it with you rather than at you.
I appreciate that. Where would you like to start? Probably the back, since that is the oldest of it.
The back, yes. This is the chronic pain since your neck operation.
That is right, the cervical disc prolapse, operated in 2017.
And honestly, the pain has just carried on regardless.
Despite taking the ibumetin and the panadil regularly?
Despite both, and I do take them properly. That is the frustrating part.
And then the anti-inflammatory gave me reflux on top.
Which is why you are on pantoprazole for that.
Exactly, yes.
Yes. So one thing patching up the other, if you see what I mean.
I do. And your asthma is being followed at the pulmonary outpatient clinic.
It is, and that side of things is genuinely fine.
They keep an eye on it, and I have no complaints there.
Good. Then the menopausal symptoms, which you are taking Activel for.
Yes, and my hands have started aching as well, which is newer.
I did wonder about arthritis.
Osteoarthritis is what is suspected there, yes.
Anything else troubling you?
Constipation, I am afraid.
And I should be honest and say I still smoke.
Thank you for saying so.
Let me examine you, and then I will tell you what I find.
Please do.
You seem generally unaffected.
Your gait and standing are normal.
I can feel muscle tension in your neck and shoulders.
That tension is exactly where it always sits.
Right across there.
So, to summarize.
Chronic pain, stable asthma, chronic reflux, and you are perimenopausal with a need for treatment.
And the hands, and the constipation, and the smoking.
Osteoarthritis, constipation, and nicotine, yes.
All noted.
Now, what would you like to do about the neck and shoulder tension?
If you are about to say physiotherapy, I would rather not.
I have thought about it, and it is not for me.
Then we will not refer to it.
It is for you.
For the pain, you continue the anti-inflammatory with the stomach protection alongside it.
And is there anything I need to come back for?
An annual check of your blood pressure.
Does that plan sit right with you?
It does.
And I will say, that check-in screen at reception nearly defeated me on the way in.
You are not the first to tell me that today.
Well, I got there in the end.
Thank you, Dr. Villidsen.
